prior_verdict_overturned: Two prior verify attempts on this run returned `regressed` over a 9-vs-25 TPASS count for the target test. I have reproduced the root cause independently and confirmed it is a pre-existing harness artifact, not a kernel regression. (1) In a debug boot with scratch instrumentation I ran timer_create01 directly in-guest alongside kirk's own run, and captured both outputs in the same boot. Ground truth: exit=0, 3658 bytes, 25 TPASS, 15 TCONF, well-formed Summary block, and TINFO lines confirming all five notify types ran including SIGEV_THREAD, so the test does NOT exit early and the fix's target code path IS exercised. kirk's JSON report for the same test in the same boot: status=pass, passed=9, logbytes=1277, no Summary block, stdout ends mid-word at 'TPASS: Timer successfully created f', cut at exactly 1277 bytes. (2) Control proving pre-existing: confstr01 (already enabled at all.txt line 141, runs in CI today, entirely unrelated to timers since the patch only touches sys_timer_create + create_timer in timer_create.rs). Same boot ground truth: 2817 bytes, 34 TPASS. kirk's report: passed=14, logbytes=1277, no Summary block, cut mid-token at 'POSIX_V7_ILP32_OFFBIG_CFLAG'. chmod01 (2140 bytes, 32 TPASS) was captured completely and counted correctly as 32. The patch cannot affect confstr01's capture, so the undercount is pre-existing. Both truncated captures landed at exactly 1277 bytes = 1024 + 253, i.e. 2 read chunks. (3) Mechanism located in libkirk/channels/shell.py:177-187: the read loop breaks when _process_alive() returns False rather than on EOF, discarding bytes still buffered when the child exits. Host-side stress of that exact loop against 'cat <bigfile>' across 150 trials: 2140/2817/3658-byte payloads zero truncations, 8000-byte payload 5 truncations with the shortest capture exactly 3072 bytes = 3 x 1024, a read-chunk boundary. Then ltp.py read_result loses the Summary block and falls back to stdout.count('TPASS') with skipped from stdout.count('TSKIP'), while LTP emits TCONF not TSKIP, producing the 9-passed/0-skipped signature. (4) The fix is sound: timer_create01 passes the gate (failed/broken/warnings = 0), is green in the full-suite run (status=pass), and the SIGEV_THREAD notify type does execute. The 9-vs-25 discrepancy is a reporting-fidelity issue, not a kernel correctness defect, and it is not caused by this patch.
